legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan parole orders can be amended in writing
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan law provides that amendments to parole orders must be in writing, and notice must be given to the parolee before an amendment takes effect.
legal_rules.qualifications: Read the actual order and any amendments. Contact the supervising authority about disputed or missing paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Individualized Michigan parole conditions
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan parole is governed by a written parole order and may include individualized supervision conditions.
legal_rules.qualifications: Do not infer reporting deadlines, curfews or freedom to travel; follow the signed current order.

legal_rules.rule_title: Restitution may be included in Michigan parole order
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan law requires specified court-ordered restitution terms in applicable parole orders.
legal_rules.qualifications: Payment amounts and schedules come from actual court and parole paperwork; ask about formal adjustment or assistance if unaffordable.

legal_rules.rule_title: Additional residence reporting can apply in Michigan
legal_rules.plain_language: Specific individuals subject to Michigan registration requirements must provide the proposed residence location before release.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only applies if the statute and any court/supervision conditions apply to that person.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan voting restriction applies while confined under sentence
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan Election Law prohibits voting while a person is legally convicted, sentenced, and confined in jail or prison.
legal_rules.qualifications: This provision alone does not decide all voter-registration facts; check Michigan election guidance and any applicable federal requirements.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan no-fee state ID: housing insecurity
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan Secretary of State lists housing insecurity as a no-fee state-ID eligibility category, with a public-service-agency verification letter and HMIS photo ID requirements.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applicants without these exact documents should seek a housing-service provider and ask SOS about acceptable alternatives. This is not a blanket waiver.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan no-fee state ID: certain benefit recipients
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan SOS lists recipients of FIP, SDA, SSDI or SSI as potentially eligible for a no-fee ID when official program proof is provided.
legal_rules.qualifications: Other benefits do not automatically qualify; confirm the exact accepted program and evidence.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan no-fee state ID: veterans
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan SOS lists veterans as eligible for a no-fee standard ID with specified service records or veteran identification.
legal_rules.qualifications: Confirm all identity, legal presence and residency requirements with SOS first.

legal_rules.rule_title: Other Michigan no-fee state ID categories
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan SOS lists age 65+, legally blind, some voluntary license surrender and specified medical license-action situations as possible no-fee ID pathways.
legal_rules.qualifications: Each category has distinct proof requirements and some first-time applicants must visit an office.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan public benefits applications
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan MDHHS provides applications for food assistance, Medicaid and other support; individual eligibility is determined by the agency.
legal_rules.qualifications: A denied application can carry reconsideration and fair-hearing rights depending on program; get a written notice and deadline.

legal_rules.rule_title: California 2026 certified birth record price
legal_rules.plain_language: California Department of Public Health lists a $31 fee per standard certified birth record effective January 1, 2026; the CDC directory still lists $29.
legal_rules.qualifications: County methods, identity requirements and shipping costs may differ. Ask the issuer to confirm current total before sending money.
legal_rules.statute_citation: CA Health & Safety Code 103625; CDPH 2026 fee schedule

legal_rules.rule_title: California no-fee birth certificate for qualifying unhoused residents
legal_rules.plain_language: California CDPH states that qualified people experiencing homelessness can request one fee-exempt certified birth record using the homelessness verification affidavit.
legal_rules.qualifications: Eligibility and verification must be confirmed; check with state registrar or the county where born. Not automatic from a housing statement.

legal_rules.rule_title: California DMV no-fee state ID for qualifying homelessness
legal_rules.plain_language: California DMV describes no-fee identification for qualifying people experiencing homelessness when a qualified organization verifies status on form DL 933.
legal_rules.qualifications: A signed eligibility verification and the DMV identity documentation are needed; confirm with a verifier and DMV before travel.

legal_rules.rule_title: California DMV reduced-fee ID for qualifying low income
legal_rules.plain_language: California DMV describes a reduced-fee ID program requiring qualifying income verification on form DL 937 from a qualified program.
legal_rules.qualifications: Do not claim reduced price without confirmed eligibility and the correct form; check current reduced fee and DMV documentation.

legal_rules.rule_title: Washington DOL ID help for people experiencing homelessness
legal_rules.plain_language: Washington Department of Licensing describes one no-cost state identification card per lifetime for eligible people experiencing homelessness, with reduced-cost options for some applicants.
legal_rules.qualifications: One-per-lifetime rule and identity-document requirements apply. A public-assistance/WIC pathway can involve a reduced fee rather than free ID; confirm before ordering.

legal_rules.rule_title: Oregon no-fee ID for eligible unhoused individuals
legal_rules.plain_language: Oregon law provides no-fee non-REAL-ID state identification and specified replacements for qualifying individuals experiencing homelessness.
legal_rules.qualifications: A determination of homelessness and other evidence are required; REAL ID supplementary fees and valid driving-privilege rules may apply. Confirm with DMV.

legal_rules.rule_title: New York no-fee non-driver ID for certain public-assistance recipients
legal_rules.plain_language: New York State OTDA has issued guidance on DMV no-fee non-driver ID cards for eligible public-assistance and SNAP recipients.
legal_rules.qualifications: Qualifying benefits, proof and application method must be confirmed with DMV; original ID and renewal procedures may differ, and not everyone on benefits qualifies.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: initial reporting
legal_rules.plain_language: Published federal standard language specifies initial probation office reporting within 72 hours of prison release unless instructed otherwise.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: subsequent reporting
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language says follow directions for ongoing reporting after the first probation-office report.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: travel outside district
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language bars knowingly leaving the authorized federal judicial district without prior court or probation officer permission.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: truthful responses
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language requires truthful answers to probation officer questions.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: approved residence and notice
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language calls for an officer-approved home and notice before changes; the standard text describes 10 days advance notice when feasible and a 72-hour alternative for unforeseen changes.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: home visits
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language describes officer home visits and taking prohibited items observed in plain view.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: work and job changes
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language describes full-time lawful employment or job search unless excused, plus notice about job changes.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: certain contacts
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language limits interaction with persons engaged in criminal activity and addresses contact with known people convicted of felonies.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: law enforcement contact notice
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language calls for notifying probation officer within 72 hours of arrest or questioning by law enforcement.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: firearms and weapons
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language restricts owning, possessing or accessing firearms, ammunition, destructive devices or dangerous weapons.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: confidential sources
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language requires court permission before acting as a confidential human source or informant.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: risk notification
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language can require notifying another person or organization of a specified risk when directed.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: follow supervision instructions
legal_rules.plain_language: Published standard language requires following the probation officer’s instructions related to supervision conditions.
legal_rules.qualifications: Only if imposed in the signed judgment or valid modification; an officer or court may give different specific instructions. Confirm your own paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Interstate supervision transfers: obtain permission before travel
legal_rules.plain_language: ICAOS advises people not to travel to a receiving state after transfer approval until they have contacted the supervising officer and ensured necessary permission was granted.
legal_rules.qualifications: ICAOS governs covered state-to-state transfers, not ordinary federal supervised release; ask the compact office and officer.

legal_rules.rule_title: Interstate transfer: arrival and departure notifications
legal_rules.plain_language: ICAOS Rule 4.105 addresses departure and arrival notifications for covered state-to-state supervision transfers.
legal_rules.qualifications: This rule describes the interstate notification process; your individual reporting instructions still govern your actions.

legal_rules.rule_title: Social Security card replacement costs $0
legal_rules.plain_language: Social Security Administration provides replacement cards without an application fee.
legal_rules.qualifications: Documents and eligibility differ; do not pay a third party for the card itself.

legal_rules.rule_title: Birth certificate comes from place of birth
legal_rules.plain_language: The issuing vital-records office is in the state or territory where the birth occurred.
legal_rules.qualifications: State fees, identification proof, record availability and access limitations differ.

legal_rules.rule_title: Voting after a felony conviction: District of Columbia
legal_rules.plain_language: NCSL reports this jurisdiction does not disenfranchise a person solely due to a felony conviction, including during incarceration.
legal_rules.qualifications: Registration, residence, citizenship, age and individual voting procedures still apply. Confirm with your election administrator.
legal_rules.statute_citation: DC law on voting rights for incarcerated residents (see NCSL state profile)

legal_rules.rule_title: Voting after a felony conviction: Wyoming
legal_rules.plain_language: NCSL places this state in its complex restoration category: conviction type, sentence completion, an additional application or waiting period can change when voting rights return.
legal_rules.qualifications: Do not assume voting is either allowed or barred based on incarceration alone; obtain individualized eligibility review with an election official or legal-aid organization.

legal_rules.rule_title: California state parole: first report
legal_rules.plain_language: CDCR states that a person on California state parole must report to the parole agent within one day of release from prison or jail.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to California state parole only; local supervision, special conditions and the signed parole form may add or change restrictions.
legal_rules.statute_citation: CDCR Division of Adult Parole Operations: Parole Conditions

legal_rules.rule_title: California state parole: ongoing reports
legal_rules.plain_language: CDCR states that the parolee must report when directed by their parole agent.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to California state parole only; local supervision, special conditions and the signed parole form may add or change restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: California state parole: address before move
legal_rules.plain_language: California CDCR requires the parolee to give the agent the new address before moving and to provide living and work addresses.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to California state parole only; local supervision, special conditions and the signed parole form may add or change restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: California state parole: report job change
legal_rules.plain_language: CDCR says to notify the parole agent within three days after a new job or a change of work location.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to California state parole only; local supervision, special conditions and the signed parole form may add or change restrictions. Confirm actual timing and exceptions in the signed conditions.

legal_rules.rule_title: California state parole: trips beyond 50 miles
legal_rules.plain_language: CDCR instructs state parolees to obtain their parole agent’s approval before traveling more than 50 miles from their residence.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to California state parole only; local supervision, special conditions and the signed parole form may add or change restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: California state parole: extended out-of-county trip
legal_rules.plain_language: CDCR instructs parolees to obtain a travel pass before leaving their county for more than two days.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to California state parole only; local supervision, special conditions and the signed parole form may add or change restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: California state parole: leaving California
legal_rules.plain_language: CDCR instructs state parolees to obtain a travel pass before leaving California and to carry it while traveling.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to California state parole only; local supervision, special conditions and the signed parole form may add or change restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: Texas: report as directed
legal_rules.plain_language: TDCJ lists reporting as instructed by the supervising parole officer among its general parole conditions.
legal_rules.qualifications: Texas parole or mandatory-supervision FAQ; refer to the release certificate and individual parole officer for the applicable rule and timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: Texas: written permission to move
legal_rules.plain_language: TDCJ says parolees should obtain the parole officer’s written permission before changing residence.
legal_rules.qualifications: Texas parole or mandatory-supervision FAQ; refer to the release certificate and individual parole officer for the applicable rule and timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: Texas: written permission before leaving state
legal_rules.plain_language: TDCJ says parolees should obtain the parole officer’s written permission before leaving Texas.
legal_rules.qualifications: Texas parole or mandatory-supervision FAQ; refer to the release certificate and individual parole officer for the applicable rule and timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: Texas: how often to report
legal_rules.plain_language: TDCJ says the reporting frequency depends on the supervision level and is discussed at the initial parole office visit.
legal_rules.qualifications: Texas parole or mandatory-supervision FAQ; refer to the release certificate and individual parole officer for the applicable rule and timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: New York: establish reporting schedule
legal_rules.plain_language: At the initial interview, New York DOCCS says the parole officer reviews the release agreement, residence and programs and establishes the next reporting time.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to NY DOCCS community supervision; high-risk classification, individual conditions and the written release agreement may change obligations.

legal_rules.rule_title: New York: initial weekly reporting
legal_rules.plain_language: New York DOCCS says parolees are generally required to report weekly upon release; office reporting frequency may later change by risk level and compliance.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to NY DOCCS community supervision; high-risk classification, individual conditions and the written release agreement may change obligations.

legal_rules.rule_title: New York: in-state travel may be allowed without extra approval
legal_rules.plain_language: DOCCS describes in-state travel without advance officer approval for people who are not high risk and have no concerns requiring officer review.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to NY DOCCS community supervision; high-risk classification, individual conditions and the written release agreement may change obligations. This is CONDITIONAL, not a blanket permission. Ask the PO about geographic restrictions first.

legal_rules.rule_title: New York: proposed residence reviewed
legal_rules.plain_language: DOCCS describes review of proposed living arrangements and discussion of residence with the officer at the initial report.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to NY DOCCS community supervision; high-risk classification, individual conditions and the written release agreement may change obligations.

legal_rules.rule_title: New York: employment support and expectations
legal_rules.plain_language: DOCCS says parolees who can work are expected to obtain and maintain employment and may receive employment-related services.
legal_rules.qualifications: Applies to NY DOCCS community supervision; high-risk classification, individual conditions and the written release agreement may change obligations.

legal_rules.rule_title: Georgia: follow supervision instructions
legal_rules.plain_language: The Georgia State Board says parolees must answer truthfully and follow instructions from community supervision officers.
legal_rules.qualifications: Georgia state parole conditions; special conditions may impose additional restrictions, and probation on a split sentence is separate.

legal_rules.rule_title: Georgia: residence changes need permission
legal_rules.plain_language: The Georgia Parole Board says the parolee may not change residence without first getting the community supervision officer’s permission.
legal_rules.qualifications: Georgia state parole conditions; special conditions may impose additional restrictions, and probation on a split sentence is separate.

legal_rules.rule_title: Georgia: no travel outside the state without permission
legal_rules.plain_language: The Georgia Parole Board says a parolee may not leave the state of residence, even briefly, without prior officer permission.
legal_rules.qualifications: Georgia state parole conditions; special conditions may impose additional restrictions, and probation on a split sentence is separate.

legal_rules.rule_title: Georgia: work or assigned education plan
legal_rules.plain_language: The Georgia Parole Board describes participation in an officer-developed rehabilitation plan, including work, and an education alternative for some people unable to maintain reliable employment.
legal_rules.qualifications: Georgia state parole conditions; special conditions may impose additional restrictions, and probation on a split sentence is separate.

legal_rules.rule_title: Wisconsin: monthly written reports and check-ins
legal_rules.plain_language: Wisconsin DOC rules direct supervisees to submit a monthly written report and attend other reporting appointments as directed.
legal_rules.qualifications: Wisconsin DOC standard community supervision rules; agent directives, sentencing type and court orders may add restrictions.
legal_rules.statute_citation: Wisconsin DOC: Standard Rules of Community Supervision

legal_rules.rule_title: Wisconsin: prior approval to move
legal_rules.plain_language: Wisconsin DOC says supervisees must get their agent’s approval before changing residence; in an emergency, they must notify the agent within 72 hours.
legal_rules.qualifications: Wisconsin DOC standard community supervision rules; agent directives, sentencing type and court orders may add restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: Wisconsin: prior approval for job change
legal_rules.plain_language: Wisconsin DOC says to get agent approval before changing employment, with an emergency notification provision.
legal_rules.qualifications: Wisconsin DOC standard community supervision rules; agent directives, sentencing type and court orders may add restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: Wisconsin: permit before leaving state
legal_rules.plain_language: Wisconsin DOC says supervisees must obtain agent approval and a travel permit before leaving Wisconsin.
legal_rules.qualifications: Wisconsin DOC standard community supervision rules; agent directives, sentencing type and court orders may add restrictions.

legal_rules.rule_title: Oregon: reporting set by written supervision conditions
legal_rules.plain_language: ORS 144.102 provides that post-prison supervision conditions are specified in writing and may require reporting to the officer as directed.
legal_rules.qualifications: Oregon post-prison supervision (ORS 144.102); it differs from legacy Oregon parole (ORS 144.270), and special conditions and local authorities may apply.

legal_rules.rule_title: Oregon: written conditions and residence limits
legal_rules.plain_language: ORS 144.102 requires written supervision conditions, and certain residence/county restrictions may apply under subsection (7) and special conditions.
legal_rules.qualifications: Oregon post-prison supervision (ORS 144.102); it differs from legacy Oregon parole (ORS 144.270), and special conditions and local authorities may apply. Do not infer a six-month county rule without determining which part of ORS 144.102(7) applies and whether an exception applies.

legal_rules.rule_title: Oregon: protection for labor-dispute job refusals
legal_rules.plain_language: ORS 144.102(6) provides that refusing to seek or accept work at a site with a current labor dispute is not itself a post-prison supervision violation.
legal_rules.qualifications: Oregon post-prison supervision (ORS 144.102); it differs from legacy Oregon parole (ORS 144.270), and special conditions and local authorities may apply.

legal_rules.rule_title: Oregon: supervision authority can set special conditions
legal_rules.plain_language: ORS 144.102(4) authorizes additional conditions for individual circumstances; the assigned written conditions must be reviewed.
legal_rules.qualifications: Oregon post-prison supervision (ORS 144.102); it differs from legacy Oregon parole (ORS 144.270), and special conditions and local authorities may apply.

legal_rules.rule_title: Illinois: board sets parole and MSR conditions
legal_rules.plain_language: 730 ILCS 5/3-3-7 directs that parole and mandatory-supervised-release conditions are set by the Prisoner Review Board within applicable law.
legal_rules.qualifications: Illinois parole or mandatory supervised release; law distinguishes required conditions and additional board conditions. Check the version in force and individual paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Illinois: work or education may require authorization
legal_rules.plain_language: Illinois law provides for certain employment, study and training approvals or notifications as conditions of release; check applicability to your signed conditions.
legal_rules.qualifications: Illinois parole or mandatory supervised release; law distinguishes required conditions and additional board conditions. Check the version in force and individual paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: Illinois: residence may be subject to supervision
legal_rules.plain_language: Illinois parole/MSR law allows conditions addressing where a person lives and other restrictions set by the review board.
legal_rules.qualifications: Illinois parole or mandatory supervised release; law distinguishes required conditions and additional board conditions. Check the version in force and individual paperwork.

legal_rules.rule_title: North Carolina: report as directed
legal_rules.plain_language: G.S. 15A-1368.4 lists reporting to the post-release supervision officer at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner as directed among potential conditions.
legal_rules.qualifications: North Carolina post-release supervision under G.S. 15A-1368.4; probation rules and older parole may differ. Individual commission/officer conditions control.

legal_rules.rule_title: North Carolina: work or vocational study may be a condition
legal_rules.plain_language: North Carolina law allows conditions requiring suitable employment, study or vocational training on post-release supervision.
legal_rules.qualifications: North Carolina post-release supervision under G.S. 15A-1368.4; probation rules and older parole may differ. Individual commission/officer conditions control.

legal_rules.rule_title: North Carolina: residential program as possible condition
legal_rules.plain_language: G.S. 15A-1368.4 permits a requirement to attend or reside in certain rehabilitation or residential facilities as an imposed condition.
legal_rules.qualifications: North Carolina post-release supervision under G.S. 15A-1368.4; probation rules and older parole may differ. Individual commission/officer conditions control.

legal_rules.rule_title: Ohio: sample standard form says report next business day
legal_rules.plain_language: The Ohio APA published form instructs supervisees to report in person by the next business day after release from custody.
legal_rules.qualifications: Ohio 2013 published sample Conditions of Supervision form; age of source requires reconfirmation against the individual signed current form and parole officer.

legal_rules.rule_title: Ohio: sample form says get approval before residence change
legal_rules.plain_language: The Ohio APA sample supervision form includes permission before changing residence as an officer instruction.
legal_rules.qualifications: Ohio 2013 published sample Conditions of Supervision form; age of source requires reconfirmation against the individual signed current form and parole officer.

legal_rules.rule_title: Ohio: sample form requires written out-of-state permit
legal_rules.plain_language: The Ohio APA sample form says to obtain a written travel permit before leaving Ohio.
legal_rules.qualifications: Ohio 2013 published sample Conditions of Supervision form; age of source requires reconfirmation against the individual signed current form and parole officer.

legal_rules.rule_title: Washington: in-state county travel policy with exceptions
legal_rules.plain_language: Washington DOC policy 380.650 generally calls for a signed in-state permit for travel outside the county of residence, but identifies exceptions for certain lower-risk and board-supervised people.
legal_rules.qualifications: Washington DOC policy 380.650 revised 2024; travel categories have explicit exceptions, and court/board conditions may be stricter. Do not apply to someone covered by the listed exceptions without checking their classification and officer instructions.

legal_rules.rule_title: Washington: eligible out-of-state travel permits
legal_rules.plain_language: Washington DOC policy 380.650 permits case managers to authorize eligible individuals for out-of-state travel up to 31 days; it is not automatic approval.
legal_rules.qualifications: Washington DOC policy 380.650 revised 2024; travel categories have explicit exceptions, and court/board conditions may be stricter.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: initial reporting within 72 hours
legal_rules.plain_language: The U.S. Courts standard supervised-release language directs the person to report within 72 hours of release unless their probation officer specifies a different location or time.
legal_rules.qualifications: Federal standard-condition model language, not an individual federal judgment. Applies only when actually imposed and not superseded by the sentencing court or later order.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: reporting afterward
legal_rules.plain_language: Federal model language directs people to report on the schedule specified by the federal court or probation officer after the initial report.
legal_rules.qualifications: Federal standard-condition model language, not an individual federal judgment. Applies only when actually imposed and not superseded by the sentencing court or later order.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: leaving authorized district
legal_rules.plain_language: Federal model language requires permission before knowingly leaving the authorized federal judicial district.
legal_rules.qualifications: Federal standard-condition model language, not an individual federal judgment. Applies only when actually imposed and not superseded by the sentencing court or later order.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: housing changes
legal_rules.plain_language: Federal standard language requires an approved residence and ordinarily ten days advance notice of changes to residence or household; for unforeseeable changes, notice within 72 hours of learning of the change.
legal_rules.qualifications: Federal standard-condition model language, not an individual federal judgment. Applies only when actually imposed and not superseded by the sentencing court or later order.

legal_rules.rule_title: Federal standard condition: work and notifying changes
legal_rules.plain_language: Federal standard language calls for lawful full-time work (at least 30 hours weekly) unless excused, plus notice of job changes in advance where possible.
legal_rules.qualifications: Federal standard-condition model language, not an individual federal judgment. Applies only when actually imposed and not superseded by the sentencing court or later order.

legal_rules.rule_title: Pennsylvania: report and follow parole staff instructions
legal_rules.plain_language: Pennsylvania parole regulation 37 Pa. Code §63.4 sets reporting and continuing contact with parole supervision staff among general conditions.
legal_rules.qualifications: Pennsylvania general state parole regulation 37 Pa. Code §63.4. A proposed change was published in 2026; confirm the current effective rule and signed conditions before relying on any timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: Pennsylvania: live at approved residence
legal_rules.plain_language: The Pennsylvania regulation requires parolees to live at the approved residence and obtain written permission before moving.
legal_rules.qualifications: Pennsylvania general state parole regulation 37 Pa. Code §63.4. A proposed change was published in 2026; confirm the current effective rule and signed conditions before relying on any timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: Pennsylvania: notify employment status changes
legal_rules.plain_language: The Pennsylvania parole regulation lists notification of employment and education status changes; verify timing in your official conditions because proposed regulatory amendments were announced in 2026.
legal_rules.qualifications: Pennsylvania general state parole regulation 37 Pa. Code §63.4. A proposed change was published in 2026; confirm the current effective rule and signed conditions before relying on any timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: Pennsylvania: permission for travel outside reporting district
legal_rules.plain_language: Pennsylvania §63.4 addresses departure from the assigned reporting district and written permission; obtain direction from the supervising officer and check the updated official text.
legal_rules.qualifications: Pennsylvania general state parole regulation 37 Pa. Code §63.4. A proposed change was published in 2026; confirm the current effective rule and signed conditions before relying on any timing.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan: parole agents coordinate housing needs
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan DOC says parole agents coordinate services including housing and employment; the residence may also be restricted by individual orders.
legal_rules.qualifications: Michigan state parole, not local court probation or federal supervision; signed parole order and supervising officer are controlling.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan: parole agent can connect employment services
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan DOC says agents coordinate employment-related services in the community; a particular workplace or schedule may still require individual approval.
legal_rules.qualifications: Michigan state parole, not local court probation or federal supervision; signed parole order and supervising officer are controlling.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan: review the parole order for duties
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan law provides for individualized written conditions and amendments; confirm reporting place and deadline from the parole order.
legal_rules.qualifications: Michigan state parole, not local court probation or federal supervision; signed parole order and supervising officer are controlling.

legal_rules.rule_title: Florida: check your release authority and supervising officer
legal_rules.plain_language: Florida DOC says correctional officers enforce statutory conditions and special conditions imposed by the court or releasing authority; reporting details depend on supervision type.
legal_rules.qualifications: Florida DOC supervises several distinct release types: parole, conditional release, probation and community control are not interchangeable.

legal_rules.rule_title: Florida: field contacts may occur at residence or work
legal_rules.plain_language: Florida DOC states that supervision includes field contacts at residences, workplaces, and other locations; do not treat this as a statewide moving-permission rule.
legal_rules.qualifications: Florida DOC supervises several distinct release types: parole, conditional release, probation and community control are not interchangeable.

legal_rules.rule_title: New Jersey: staff review release conditions before release
legal_rules.plain_language: New Jersey’s Parole Board says parole counselors or officers review conditions with the person and develop a discharge plan before release.
legal_rules.qualifications: New Jersey state parole. Signed standard and individual special conditions must be checked before acting.
legal_rules.statute_citation: NJ State Parole Board Release Division

legal_rules.rule_title: Indiana: residence approval in certain supervision cases
legal_rules.plain_language: Indiana DOC explains that some supervised individuals, particularly with specialized registration conditions, must remain at an approved residence unless permission is obtained.
legal_rules.qualifications: Indiana state parole; webpage also describes specialized supervision populations. Do not generalize specialized rules to all parolees.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan MDOC travel restrictions policy
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan Department of Corrections Policy Directive 06.04.110 describes travel restrictions and approval procedures for probationers and parolees. Whether you need permission for a particular trip depends on your order, destination and MDOC process.
legal_rules.qualifications: Never treat the policy as a blanket travel permit. Read your own order; ask the supervising officer before travel if your restrictions or requirements are uncertain.

legal_rules.rule_title: Michigan: required evidence for a first state ID
legal_rules.plain_language: Michigan Secretary of State lists evidence of legal presence, identity, Social Security number or applicable ineligibility letter, and Michigan residence as requirements to apply for a first ID.
legal_rules.qualifications: Ask Secretary of State what alternative evidence is accepted when you have no standard proof of address or your name changed. A state ID is not a driver license.
legal_rules.statute_citation: Michigan Secretary of State first-time license or ID

legal_rules.rule_title: Interstate compact: reporting instructions can control interstate movement
legal_rules.plain_language: The Interstate Commission provides reporting-instruction processes for certain state-supervised people transferring between states. These procedures are case-specific, not automatic permission to cross a state line or relocate.
legal_rules.qualifications: Check whether ICAOS applies to your type of supervision. Consult the sending state and supervising authority and obtain the actual reporting instructions/approval before relocating.

assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Jackson County residents; support depends on intake and funds
assistance_programs.intake_process: Call (517) 782-9766 ext 1; hours Mondays and Thursdays 10–2

assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Service area and program-specific requirements vary
assistance_programs.intake_process: Call 211 or 866-561-2500, or search by ZIP

assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Only listed qualifying categories with proof
assistance_programs.intake_process: Check official no-fee ID guide before visiting

assistance_programs.program_name: Catholic Charities Washtenaw County Region 9 Offender Success
assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Referral-based; currently limited to MDOC parole participants
assistance_programs.intake_process: Ask MDOC parole agent for referral

assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Jackson County births only; requester ID and eligibility requirements are specified by county; first certified copy listed at $15.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Call or use county clerk request information before visiting; 120 W Michigan Ave, 12th floor, Jackson.

assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Jackson County housing assessment and assistance; financial help depends on funding and assessment.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Request a housing needs assessment; 1214 Greenwood Ave, Jackson.

assistance_programs.program_name: Legal Services of South Central Michigan — Jackson
assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Free civil legal services subject to income and case eligibility. Does not automatically represent criminal parole cases.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Call Jackson intake; 540 N Jackson St, Jackson.

assistance_programs.program_name: Michigan Works! Southeast — Jackson Service Center
assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Career-seeker support; some training/funding programs have separate eligibility and priority rules.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Contact Jackson Service Center; 209 E Washington Ave, Jackson.

assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Michigan public assistance applications; program-specific household, residence, income and other rules apply.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Apply online through MI Bridges, seek paper application at local MDHHS office if necessary.

assistance_programs.program_name: Michigan State Housing Assessment Resource Agencies
assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Statewide county-by-county HARA lookup; the appropriate agency and intake conditions depend on county.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Locate your county on the MSHDA HARA contact list; ask for a coordinated housing assessment.

assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Free information/referral only; does not guarantee payment or admission.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Dial 211 and ask for Jackson County transportation and document-fee options.

assistance_programs.program_name: Jackson County MDHHS — Benefits and Services
assistance_programs.eligibility_description: Jackson County residents can ask about public-assistance applications including food and health coverage. Qualification varies by program and household.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Apply through MI Bridges or contact the county office.

assistance_programs.program_name: Michigan Department of Corrections — Reentry Services
assistance_programs.eligibility_description: MDOC lists reentry services for eligible persons, with availability based on status and location. Ask your parole agent for available local services.
assistance_programs.intake_process: Discuss eligibility and local provider availability with the assigned parole agent.

aid_referral_networks.eligibility_summary: Local providers have independent eligibility and funding limits.
aid_referral_networks.action_text: Search ZIP/county or call 211 and ask specifically about vital documents and transportation.

aid_referral_networks.eligibility_summary: Income limits, case types and intake capacity vary; generally civil legal aid, not guaranteed criminal representation.
aid_referral_networks.action_text: Search city or address for a nearby civil legal aid provider and ask about benefits appeal or housing denial.

aid_referral_networks.eligibility_summary: Free career help; available specialized programs depend on location and eligibility.
aid_referral_networks.action_text: Find the nearest AJC and ask about justice-impacted employment programs, training and supportive services.

aid_referral_networks.eligibility_summary: Resource directory, not a direct funding guarantee; providers set their own requirements.
aid_referral_networks.action_text: Search shelters and local housing entry points by location.

aid_referral_networks.eligibility_summary: Applications and eligibility are administered separately; conviction-specific rules may apply.
aid_referral_networks.action_text: Screen for food, health and other benefits; ask the agency for a written denial and hearing rights.

aid_referral_networks.eligibility_summary: Fee waivers and identity evidence are state-specific.
aid_referral_networks.action_text: Open your state motor vehicle agency; ask about no-fee ID, alternate proof and release documents.

aid_referral_networks.eligibility_summary: Issuing office in state of birth; cost and acceptable proof vary.
aid_referral_networks.action_text: Select the state where you were born and ask about fee exemptions or paper ordering.

eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask the agency exactly which alternate proofs, letters or witness/attestation methods it accepts.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Existing expired ID; facility release documents; HMIS ID and service-provider letter where accepted; replace Social Security record; request benefits record.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: No document substitute is universally accepted.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: I cannot obtain my birth certificate
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask the birth-state office what identity and relationship evidence it accepts and whether a waiver/indigent program exists.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Check if an authorized person may request it; county clerk where permitted; legal aid for record errors; local fee assistance.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: Third-party ordering may cost more and offer no eligibility shortcut.

eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask whether shelter mail, a program address, a written statement or other residency proof is accepted.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Contact shelter or case manager for approved residency letter; request local housing identification rules.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: A supervised residence may still need advance approval.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: I cannot pay document or travel fees
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask about the exact fee waiver or sponsor application; request a statement of how much is needed.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Apply for an eligible no-fee ID, SSA card at zero cost, local vital-record funding, a bus-pass grant, or provider-paid document fees.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: A fee waiver cannot be presumed until agency confirmation.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: I cannot get to an appointment
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask the agency whether a remote appointment, transportation voucher or schedule change is permitted.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Call 211, ask supervision office about transport or reasonable accommodation, contact transit accessibility services.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: Never assume absence is excused without confirming with responsible agency.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: They say I must be on parole but I am not
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask for the precise funding/referral eligibility rule and the name of the program sponsor.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Try general work centers, housing services, faith/community groups, county reentry networks or non-MDOC funding.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: Referral-only grants may genuinely be restricted to specific groups.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: My county or ZIP disqualifies me
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask which agency serves your address and whether the provider can warm-transfer you.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: County 211 entry point, local community action agency, nearby but jurisdiction-eligible nonprofit, local legal aid.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: Do not misrepresent residence to obtain benefits.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: A program rejected me because of my record
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask for a written decision and the specific policy or law; find out about exceptions, dispute or appeal rights.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Legal aid, record-relief clinics, alternate employers/housing, rights-restoration research.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: Not every exclusion is unlawful; laws and relief vary by jurisdiction and offense.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: I need an accommodation or cannot use the online system
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask for ADA/accessibility accommodation, paper form, telephone/in-person intake or language access.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: Use public library or community case worker; request help completing forms; explore appeal assistance.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: Specific legal duties depend on organization and circumstance.

eligibility_fallbacks.blocker_title: SNAP, Medicaid or cash help was denied
eligibility_fallbacks.what_to_ask: Ask for the written notice stating the exact reason, date, and fair-hearing/appeal deadline.
eligibility_fallbacks.possible_alternatives: File a timely appeal where available; correct missing documents; apply for other eligible programs; request civil legal aid.
eligibility_fallbacks.caveat: Deadlines and rules differ by program and state; do not delay.

local_providers.name: Community Action Agency — Jackson Housing Assessment
local_providers.scope: Housing assessment and coordinated entry for Jackson County
local_providers.eligibility: Assessment is a starting point; actual assistance depends on eligibility and available resources.
local_providers.before_you_go: Call ahead, explain your housing situation, and ask what proof to bring.
local_providers.if_denied: Ask for a coordinated-entry referral, the reason, and another provider serving Jackson County.

local_providers.name: Michigan Works! Southeast — Jackson
local_providers.address: 209 E. Washington Avenue, Suite 100, Jackson, MI 49201
local_providers.scope: Career services, training referrals, job-search help
local_providers.eligibility: Core job-center assistance available; training funds and specialized programs have their own eligibility rules.
local_providers.before_you_go: Call to ask which job-search and training services are available, including help without photo ID.
local_providers.if_denied: Ask which public job-center service is open to you and whether there is another training route.

local_providers.name: Love INC of Jackson County — Document Assistance
local_providers.scope: Birth records; replacement ID; some busfare assistance
local_providers.eligibility: Jackson County residents; eligibility, documentation of need, and availability of funding vary.
local_providers.before_you_go: Call extension 1. Ask about available vital-document funding or busfare and required proof.
local_providers.if_denied: Ask for an alternate source of document help; do not assume funding is available.

local_providers.name: Jackson Area Transportation Authority (JATA)
local_providers.scope: City bus routes, Reserve-a-Ride and transportation information
local_providers.eligibility: Routes, coverage, fares, advance-reservation rules and operating hours differ by service.
local_providers.before_you_go: Call and confirm the bus route, operating time, cost and any advance reservation before making an appointment trip.
local_providers.if_denied: Ask about Reserve-a-Ride, accessibility service, or a transportation referral.

local_providers.name: Jackson County Clerk — Birth Records
local_providers.address: 120 W. Michigan Avenue, 12th Floor, Jackson, MI 49201
local_providers.scope: Certified Jackson County birth records only
local_providers.eligibility: This office maintains birth records for people born in Jackson County. Photo ID or an accepted alternative is required; DOC photo ID with recent probation or discharge papers is explicitly listed.
local_providers.before_you_go: Confirm the record is from Jackson County, the accepted identification, and the current $15 first-copy local counter fee.
local_providers.if_denied: Ask which accepted alternative ID applies. For another birthplace, use that county or birth-state vital-record office.

local_providers.name: Legal Services of South Central Michigan — Jackson
local_providers.scope: Civil legal aid for Jackson and Hillsdale counties
local_providers.eligibility: Income and matter restrictions apply; not a criminal defense or automatic parole representation service.
local_providers.before_you_go: Call during posted intake hours and ask whether the specific civil legal issue is eligible.
local_providers.if_denied: Ask about intake limitations, alternative civil legal aid, or a criminal defense referral for a criminal matter.
